```plato
    //==
    // # The contact solver — one row
    //
    // One visit to one contact point. The normal is solved first and the friction
    // cone is then bounded by the normal impulse the same visit just accumulated,
    // which is the ordering that makes friction track the load instead of lagging
    // it by an iteration.
    //
    // The clamp is on the ACCUMULATED impulse, never on the increment. Clamping
    // increments would forbid a row from undoing an over-correction an earlier row
    // made in the same pass, and over-correction is normal: each row solves its own
    // contact exactly, in ignorance of the others.

    // The impulse increment that changes the relative speed along a direction from
    // `current` to `target`, given the pair's effective mass there. A pair with no
    // mobility along that direction has an infinite effective compliance and takes
    // no impulse.
    ImpulseFor(target: Number, current: Number, effectiveMass: Number): Number
        => effectiveMass > 0.0 ? (target - current) / effectiveMass : 0.0;

    // The world after solving row `index` once for velocity: restitution along the
    // normal, then Coulomb friction in the contact plane. Precondition: the row
    // names two DIFFERENT bodies, both in range.
    SolveRow(world: RigidWorld3D, index: Integer): RigidWorld3D
    {
        var row = world.Constraints[index];
        var a0 = world.Bodies[row.BodyA.Value];
        var b0 = world.Bodies[row.BodyB.Value];

        var n = row.Normal.Vector;
        var normalIncrement = ImpulseFor(
            row.TargetSeparationSpeed,
            SeparationSpeed(a0, b0, row.Point, n),
            DirectionalMass(a0, b0, row.Point, n));
        var normalTotal = (row.NormalImpulse.Amount + normalIncrement).Max(0.0);
        var normalApplied = normalTotal - row.NormalImpulse.Amount;
        var a1 = ApplyImpulse(a0, n * -normalApplied, row.Point);
        var b1 = ApplyImpulse(b0, n * normalApplied, row.Point);

        // Both friction axes are measured against the SAME post-normal state and
        // clamped together, so the cone bound applies to the friction impulse as a
        // vector rather than to each axis alone. Solving them one after the other
        // would make friction depend on which axis `Tangent` happened to pick.
        var t = row.Tangent.Vector;
        var u = row.Bitangent.Vector;
        var tangentRaw = row.TangentImpulse.Amount + ImpulseFor(
            0.0, SeparationSpeed(a1, b1, row.Point, t), DirectionalMass(a1, b1, row.Point, t));
        var bitangentRaw = row.BitangentImpulse.Amount + ImpulseFor(
            0.0, SeparationSpeed(a1, b1, row.Point, u), DirectionalMass(a1, b1, row.Point, u));
        var frictionMagnitude = (tangentRaw.Square + bitangentRaw.Square).Sqrt;
        var frictionLimit = row.Friction * normalTotal;
        var scale = frictionMagnitude > frictionLimit && frictionMagnitude > 0.0
            ? frictionLimit / frictionMagnitude
            : 1.0;
        var tangentTotal = tangentRaw * scale;
        var bitangentTotal = bitangentRaw * scale;
        var frictionApplied = t * (tangentTotal - row.TangentImpulse.Amount)
            + u * (bitangentTotal - row.BitangentImpulse.Amount);

        return RigidWorld3D(
            ReplacedAt(
                ReplacedAt(world.Bodies, row.BodyA.Value,
                    ApplyImpulse(a1, frictionApplied.Negative, row.Point)),
                row.BodyB.Value,
                ApplyImpulse(b1, frictionApplied, row.Point)),
            ReplacedAt(world.Constraints, index, WithImpulses(row,
                Impulse.FromAmount(normalTotal),
                Impulse.FromAmount(tangentTotal),
                Impulse.FromAmount(bitangentTotal))),
            world.Gravity,
            world.TimeStep,
            world.Solver);
    }

    // The world after re-applying row `index`'s already-accumulated impulses to its
    // two bodies. Run once before the iteration begins, this is what makes warm
    // starting mean anything: the row remembers last frame's impulse, and the
    // bodies must be moving as if it had been applied before the solver measures
    // anything.
    WarmStartRow(world: RigidWorld3D, index: Integer): RigidWorld3D
    {
        var row = world.Constraints[index];
        var stored = row.Normal.Vector * row.NormalImpulse.Amount
            + row.Tangent.Vector * row.TangentImpulse.Amount
            + row.Bitangent.Vector * row.BitangentImpulse.Amount;
        return RigidWorld3D(
            ReplacedAt(
                ReplacedAt(world.Bodies, row.BodyA.Value,
                    ApplyImpulse(world.Bodies[row.BodyA.Value], stored.Negative, row.Point)),
                row.BodyB.Value,
                ApplyImpulse(world.Bodies[row.BodyB.Value], stored, row.Point)),
            world.Constraints,
            world.Gravity,
            world.TimeStep,
            world.Solver);
    }

    //==
    // # The contact solver — passes and iteration
    //
    // A pass is a fold over the row indices; the solve is a fold over the iteration
    // counter. Both thread the whole world, so both are ordinary pure functions of
    // it and either can be called on its own.

    // The indices 0 .. count - 1, the sequence both folds run over.
    Indices(count: Integer): Array<Integer>
        => MapRange(count, i => i);

    // The world with every row's stored impulse re-applied.
    WarmStart(world: RigidWorld3D): RigidWorld3D
        => Indices(world.Constraints.Count).Reduce(world, (acc, i) => WarmStartRow(acc, i));

    // One Gauss-Seidel sweep: every row solved once, in order, each seeing the
    // velocities the rows before it wrote.
    SolveVelocityPass(world: RigidWorld3D): RigidWorld3D
        => Indices(world.Constraints.Count).Reduce(world, (acc, i) => SolveRow(acc, i));

    // The velocity solve: warm start, then `VelocityIterations` sweeps. More
    // sweeps means a stiffer, less springy stack; the cost is exactly linear in the
    // count, which is why the number lives in `TimeStepSettings` where a caller can
    // trade it.
    SolveVelocities(world: RigidWorld3D): RigidWorld3D
        => Indices(world.TimeStep.VelocityIterations)
            .Reduce(WarmStart(world), (acc, i) => SolveVelocityPass(acc));

    //==
    // # The contact solver — position correction
    //
    // Overlap that the velocity solve cannot remove — because removing it is a
    // POSITION error, not a velocity one — is taken out by a second, separate solve
    // whose velocities are fictitious. The pseudo-velocities start at zero, are
    // driven by a target speed proportional to the excess penetration, and are used
    // only to displace poses; they are then discarded and never touch a body's
    // motion. This is the "split impulse" arrangement.
    //
    // Two details make it settle rather than hunt:
    //
    //   * THE SLOP. Correction is applied only to the penetration BEYOND
    //     `PenetrationSlop`. A resting contact is allowed to keep a small overlap,
    //     which is what gives collision detection something to find next frame; a
    //     solver that drives penetration to exactly zero loses the contact, regains
    //     it after the body falls back, and buzzes at the frame rate.
    //   * THE CAP. `MaxCorrectionSpeed` bounds how fast the correction may push, so
    //     a body that starts deeply inside another crawls out over several frames
    //     instead of being ejected.

    // The correction speed a penetration asks for: the excess beyond the slop,
    // scaled by the Baumgarte factor and spread over one step, capped. Zero when
    // the overlap is within the slop.
    CorrectionSpeed(penetration: Length, settings: ContactSolverSettings, seconds: Number): Number
        => ((penetration.Amount - settings.PenetrationSlop.Amount).Max(0.0)
            * settings.BaumgarteFactor / seconds)
            .Min(settings.MaxCorrectionSpeed.Amount);
```
